summary: Fourteen days of good-quality CGM data (98.7% coverage) from a diluted U200 AAPS closed-loop system show overall time-in-range of 86.0% with time-below-range of 5.1% and high glucose variability (CV 32.6%). All 655 logged insulin entries are correction boluses; zero carbohydrate or e-carb entries were logged during the period, which blocks direct validation of carb ratio and meal-bolus behavior. Two recurring daily glucose-rise windows (07:00-10:00 and 12:00-16:00 local) and two severe hypoglycemia clusters linked to closely spaced correction dosing were identified. No profile or AAPS parameter change is currently supported by the evidence; the primary actionable step is to begin logging meal carbohydrate timing and amount before attributing the recurring afternoon pattern to basal, carb ratio, insulin sensitivity factor, or automation settings.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is good (98.7%, ~5-minute cadence, 10 gaps, largest 65 minutes, no duplicates or invalid entries). The active aaps_profile was declared as authoritative for the whole period per profile_context.historical_applicability=yes. A Profile Switch event on 2026-08-13 to a 'u200 dilute basal - FLAT ISF' configuration is present in telemetry and is consistent with the current profile's single flat ISF segment and small basal values, but per instruction this telemetry linkage must not be used to override the explicit user declaration of full-period applicability; confidence in applying current numeric values to the 2026-08-07 to 2026-08-12 sub-period is lowered rather than treated as a contradiction. Zero carbohydrate entries exist across the whole 14-day period despite 655 insulin entries, all recorded as correction boluses. GLP-1 doses were noted three times and an occlusion/pump error was announced once (2026-08-19).
analysis_steps.evidence: telemetry.data_quality; representative_events profile switch and site/sensor changes; treatment_summary showing carb_entries=0 and insulin_entries=655; profile_context.historical_applicability
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No documentation reconciling the mid-period profile switch event with the single declared aaps_profile record; GLP-1 dosing not modeled as a time-varying factor; confirmed TIR range boundaries not stated in package

analysis_steps.findings: Overall time-below-range is 5.1%, above a conventional <4% target, with two severe hypoglycemia clusters (42-51 mg/dL on 2026-08-13 and 41-48 mg/dL on 2026-08-14) each following a correction bolus given during a rising or recently peaked glucose trend. Two severe hyperglycemia clusters (up to 293 mg/dL on 2026-08-15 and up to 290 mg/dL on 2026-08-18) coincide with loop logs already requesting large insulin amounts before the peak was reached. Coefficient of variation is 32.6%, indicating high glucose variability.
analysis_steps.evidence: glucose_summary; glucose_extremes; therapy_response_windows for 2026-08-13 13:05 and 2026-08-14 16:20 entries; representative_loop_statuses for 2026-08-14 18:40 and 2026-08-19 15:55
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate logging to confirm or rule out meals as excursion triggers; only a sampled subset of loop statuses provided

analysis_steps.findings: Early-night hours (00:00-02:00 local) show the highest time-below-range of the day (11.4-18.5%) while 03:00-07:00 local, under a similar or identical basal rate, show excellent control (time-in-range 89.2-98.7%). This pattern implicates residual evening insulin-on-board tail rather than the 00:00 basal rate itself, since the same or a closely related rate performs well only a few hours later. The 10:00-16:00 basal segment (0.7 U/h, dropping to 0.5 U/h at 16:00) spans the period of heaviest recurring hyperglycemia (time-above-range 14.0-32.1%, peak average 162.8 mg/dL at hour 16 local), but this cannot be separated from a possible unlogged meal effect. Several manual Temporary Targets to 135 mg/dL were used during the day and must not be conflated with the profile's own target segments when interpreting hourly time-in-range.
analysis_steps.evidence: hourly_glucose_local; aaps_profile.basal_segments; aaps_profile.target_segments; representative_events temporary targets
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No confirmed basal history prior to the 2026-08-13 profile switch; no meal timestamps to separate basal insufficiency from meal effect

analysis_steps.findings: The profile declares a single flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U for the whole day, but Dynamic ISF (enabled, 70% adjustment factor) produces effective sensitivity values ranging roughly from 27.8 to 178.7 mg/dL/U across sampled loop statuses, meaning the static profile value is only a loose anchor and outcome variability cannot be attributed to it in isolation. All insulin entries are correction boluses with zero carbohydrate entries, so the five carb ratio segments (10.5-13.2 g/U) cannot be validated against any meal-response data. A 10-hour duration of insulin action is long relative to typical rapid-acting insulin, which could plausibly extend the insulin tail behind large corrections, but the declared diluted U200 insulin strategy may independently justify slower modeled kinetics; this remains an unresolved two-sided hypothesis.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.isf_segments; aaps_profile.carb_ratio_segments; aaps_profile.dia_hours; representative_loop_statuses variable_sens values; therapy_response_windows correction-only entries
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate entries to test carb ratio; no independent documentation of the diluted-insulin pharmacokinetics assumed by the profile

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are enabled and, because carbohydrate-on-board is always zero in this dataset, UAM functions as the sole automated meal-reaction mechanism; smb_with_cob_enabled and smb_after_carbs_enabled being false are dormant rather than defective settings under this usage pattern. SMB is suppressed during six Temporary Target windows at 135 mg/dL (smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled=false); several of these follow GLP-1 dosing notes, suggesting a plausible but unconfirmed deliberate user strategy. A clear stacked-dosing sequence was found on 2026-08-14: a 0.2 U correction bolus at 16:20 followed by a 1.1 U correction bolus at 16:30, preceding the severe hypoglycemia cluster at 18:04-18:14, followed by an aggressive rebound temp basal request of 4 U/h at 18:40.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.smb_settings; representative_events temporary targets and GLP-1 notes; representative_treatments 2026-08-14 16:20 and 16:30 entries; representative_loop_statuses 2026-08-14 18:40
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Full loop-status history during the six temporary-target windows is not available in the sampled data; treatments are not tagged as manual versus algorithm-driven

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is disabled and Dynamic ISF is enabled, avoiding double sensitivity adjustment; sensitivity_ratio values of 1.0 represent a neutral Dynamic ISF adjustment at those timestamps, not disabled automation. The wide variable_sens range confirms Dynamic ISF is actively and substantially adjusting effective sensitivity, which is a plausible contributor to correction-bolus outcome variability alongside unlogged meals; the two explanations remain entangled and cannot be separated in this stage. Max basal (12 U/h) and max IOB (25 U) are far above observed usage (peak temp basal near 4 U/h via a computed safety ceiling referenced in loop reason text, peak IOB 5.935 U) and are not binding constraints.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.smb_settings.raw_settings; representative_loop_statuses sensitivity_ratio and variable_sens fields; loop reason text referencing maxSafeBasal
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No continuous loop-status log to confirm variable_sens behavior during every excursion; diluted-insulin pharmacokinetics not independently verifiable

analysis_steps.findings: No prebolus timing, immediate-bolus percentage, or e-carb strategy is declared in aaps_profile.analysis_context (meal_strategies is empty and period_exceptions and strategy_stable_for_period are null), so there is no user-declared strategy to compare against telemetry; this is a genuine declared absence, not a missing reproduction. All 655 insulin entries are correction boluses with no meal boluses or carbohydrate entries, so dosing during the two recurring rise windows (07:00-10:00 and 12:00-16:00 local) is entirely reactive. Several correction boluses in these windows are followed by continued rises (e.g., 2026-08-14 10:25) or later overcorrection into hypoglycemia (2026-08-13, 2026-08-14, 2026-08-19), consistent with unlogged meals combined with Dynamic ISF variability, but causation cannot be isolated.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate entries exist to anchor any meal event for prebolus or bolus-percentage assessment

analysis_steps.findings: No e-carb amount, start offset, duration, or extended-carb entry exists anywhere in the package (extended_carb_entries=0, average_extended_carb_duration_min=null, carb_treatment_entries empty), so this stage cannot assess absorption fit or compare e-carbs to a pump extended bolus.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No e-carb or carbohydrate entries exist to evaluate against the carbohydrate absorption model settings

analysis_steps.findings: Across all stages, the dominant limiting factor is the complete absence of carbohydrate logging, which prevents separating meal effects from basal, carb ratio, insulin sensitivity factor, duration of insulin action, and Dynamic ISF effects. No profile or AAPS parameter change is currently supported by evidence strong enough to isolate a single cause; competing explanations (unlogged meals, Dynamic ISF variability, insulin-on-board stacking, long duration of insulin action) remain entangled for both the recurring afternoon hyperglycemia and the two severe hypoglycemia clusters tied to closely spaced correction dosing. The single most useful next step is behavioral: begin carbohydrate logging in the two recurring windows before considering any numeric change, and address correction-bolus spacing as a standalone safety topic given its direct link to the two severe hypoglycemia episodes.

strengths: Overall CGM data quality is good, with 98.7% coverage and near-continuous 5-minute cadence over the full 14-day period.
Overnight hours 03:00-07:00 local show strong control, with time-in-range between 89.2% and 98.7% and minimal time-above-range.
Configured safety ceilings (max basal 12 U/h, max IOB 25 U) are not being approached by observed dosing, indicating a wide safety margin under current usage.
Autosens and Dynamic ISF are configured as mutually exclusive mechanisms without conflict, avoiding double sensitivity adjustment.
No coverage, duplicate, or invalid-entry issues were found in the glucose data quality assessment.
issues: Time-below-range is 5.1% for the period, above a conventional under-4% reference, with two severe hypoglycemia clusters (as low as 41-42 mg/dL) each following a correction bolus given during or shortly after a glucose rise.
Coefficient of variation is 32.6%, indicating high overall glucose variability across the period.

Two recurring daily glucose-rise windows (07:00-10:00 and 12:00-16:00 local) show consistent time-above-range increases (up to 32.1% at hour 16 local) that cannot currently be attributed to basal, carb ratio, or meal effects due to zero carbohydrate logging.
A stacked correction-bolus sequence on 2026-08-14 (two boluses ten minutes apart) preceded a severe hypoglycemia episode and a subsequent aggressive rebound dosing request.
An occlusion and pump error were announced on 2026-08-19, which may confound the hyperglycemia observed that day independent of any profile or automation setting.

recommendations.title: Begin logging meal carbohydrate timing and amount
recommendations.description: Zero carbohydrate entries exist across 14 days despite two recurring daily glucose-rise windows and correction-only dosing. Logging carbohydrate grams and timestamps, particularly around 07:00-10:00 and 12:00-16:00 local, is the single step most likely to allow separation of meal effects from basal, carb ratio, and insulin sensitivity factor effects in a future review.

recommendations.title: Review correction-bolus spacing with a care team before any dosing change
recommendations.description: A closely spaced pair of correction boluses on 2026-08-14 preceded a severe hypoglycemia episode and a subsequent aggressive rebound dosing request. This pattern should be discussed with a care team as a standalone safety topic, independent of any profile or automation parameter change.

recommendations.title: Hold basal segment changes for the 10:00-16:00 window pending carbohydrate data
recommendations.description: The 10:00-16:00 basal segment coincides with the largest recurring hyperglycemia burden, but a plausible unlogged meal effect has not been ruled out. Changing this segment before carbohydrate logging risks masking or overcorrecting a meal-driven pattern.

recommendations.title: Defer Dynamic ISF adjustment factor review until meal timing is separated
recommendations.description: Effective sensitivity from Dynamic ISF varies widely across the period and is entangled with possible unlogged meal effects on correction-bolus outcomes. Reviewing this setting before separating these effects risks attributing a meal-driven pattern to an automation parameter.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all current basal segments unchanged for now, including the 10:00-16:00 and 16:00 segments that coincide with the largest recurring afternoon hyperglycemia, because a plausible unlogged meal effect has not been ruled out.
profile_recommendation.rationale: The recurring 12:00-16:00 local hyperglycemia window overlaps a basal reduction to 0.5 U/h at 16:00, but zero carbohydrate entries exist to confirm whether this pattern reflects basal insufficiency, a meal effect, or both; changing basal now risks masking a meal-driven pattern or introducing a confound for future analysis.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Log carbohydrate amount and timestamp for meals occurring in the 07:00-10:00 and 12:00-16:00 local windows for 7-10 days, then re-assess whether the afternoon glucose pattern persists on days without recorded meals in that window.

Evidence is insufficient to isolate the rate as the cause; dependent on resolving correction-bolus timing effects first.

Dynamic ISF adjusts effective sensitivity across a wide range (approximately 27.8 to 178.7 mg/dL/U) around this static anchor, so outcome variability in correction boluses cannot be attributed to the flat profile value in isolation; this is also entangled with possible unlogged meal effects.

The overnight hypoglycemia pattern at hours 00:00-02:00 local resolves by hours 03:00-07:00 local under the same or a closely related target, suggesting residual insulin-on-board tail rather than the target value as the driver.

This single flat daytime target spans both well-controlled and poorly controlled hours, making it too broad to attribute the recurring afternoon pattern to the target value itself without further data.
Hour 23:00 local shows reasonable control, providing no evidence to support a change to this transition point.

A long duration of insulin action could plausibly extend the insulin tail behind large corrections and contribute to delayed hypoglycemia, but the declared diluted U200 insulin strategy may independently justify slower modeled kinetics; this is an unresolved two-sided hypothesis and DIA changes interact with other dosing decisions that should not be adjusted together.
UAM functions as the sole automated meal-reaction mechanism given zero carbohydrate logging, and no inconsistency or safety concern was found in this configuration.

Carbohydrate-on-board is always zero in this dataset, so the carb-based activation conditions are dormant rather than defective. Suppression of SMB during high temporary targets correlates plausibly with a deliberate user strategy around GLP-1 dosing notes, but this is unconfirmed and does not currently support a change.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Neither limit is binding in the observed data; peak insulin-on-board (5.935 U) and peak temp basal rates (near 4 U/h via a computed safety ceiling) remain well below these thresholds, showing no evidence of harm or insufficiency.

Autosens and Dynamic ISF are correctly configured as mutually exclusive mechanisms. The wide effective sensitivity range produced by Dynamic ISF is plausible expected behavior, but it is currently entangled with unresolved unlogged-meal effects on correction-bolus outcomes; changing this setting before separating those effects would risk attributing a meal-driven pattern to automation.
Carbohydrate-on-board is always zero throughout the period, so this model is never exercised and cannot be validated in either direction from the available data.

implementation_steps: Review this analysis with a care team or clinician before making any changes; do not modify AAPS settings automatically based on this content.

Begin logging carbohydrate amount and timestamp for meals, prioritizing the 12:00-16:00 local window first and the 07:00-10:00 local window second, for at least 7-10 days without changing any profile or AAPS setting.
Separately discuss the 2026-08-14 stacked correction-bolus and rebound-dosing pattern with a care team as a standalone safety topic, independent of any settings change.
After the carbohydrate logging period, re-run this analysis to separate meal-driven glucose patterns from basal, carb ratio, insulin sensitivity factor, and Dynamic ISF effects.
If a change becomes supported by the updated data, change only one profile or AAPS parameter at a time, and monitor glucose closely for several days before making any further change.

Only after basal, target, carb ratio, and insulin sensitivity factor findings are stabilized should Dynamic ISF adjustment factor and duration of insulin action be reviewed, since both interact with the other settings.
education: Time-below-range above roughly 4% and a coefficient of variation above 36% are commonly used reference points for glucose variability discussions with a care team, though exact thresholds should be confirmed with a clinician.

Dynamic ISF adjusts effective insulin sensitivity in real time and can produce a wide range of effective values even when the underlying profile insulin sensitivity factor stays constant; a sensitivity_ratio of 1.0 reflects a neutral adjustment at that moment, not disabled automation.
Autosens and Dynamic ISF are alternative sensitivity-adjustment mechanisms; running both together can double-adjust sensitivity, so having only one active at a time is a coherent configuration.

Diluted insulin concentrations (such as U200 dilutions) can have different absorption characteristics than standard concentrations, which may be a relevant factor when interpreting a longer duration of insulin action setting.
Closely spaced correction boluses can stack insulin-on-board in ways that are not always visible at the time of dosing, which can contribute to delayed hypoglycemia several hours later.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
TuneMyBG prepares data for review only and does not provide medical advice.
Do not change AAPS settings automatically based on this analysis; discuss any proposed change with a qualified care team first.

Given the two documented severe hypoglycemia episodes linked to correction-bolus timing, treat correction-bolus spacing as a priority safety discussion topic independent of any profile or automation setting change.

Do not change dependent insulin-delivery settings such as basal, carb ratio, insulin sensitivity factor, and duration of insulin action at the same time; verify one change at a time with close glucose monitoring.
